implementation.steve_decision: Use the new syllabus during the 2027 planning and preparation phase

course_requirements.all_outcomes: All outcomes must be programmed for 100-hour and 200-hour courses.
course_requirements.course_100_hours: At least 2 textile projects, with associated folio documentation, selected syllabus content relevant to each project, and at least one collaborative activity.
course_requirements.course_200_hours: At least 4 textile projects, with associated folio documentation, all syllabus content, and at least one collaborative activity.
course_requirements.practical_majority: Practical experiences must make up the majority of the course and should be designed to be accessible to all students.

outcomes.statement: applies design processes and safe work practices to develop textile projects
communicates ideas, concepts and processes for textile design and production
investigates and evaluates design inspiration sources and textile products
explains industry practices and innovative technologies used in textile design and production
investigates and applies construction and decorative techniques to create textile products
justifies the selection and use of materials and technologies for textile design and production
analyses relationships between textile design, production and sustainability

groups.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ textile Practices

statements.statement: Identify textile art forms created for expression, communication and Storytelling
Describe Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander textile designer Practices and products
examples: Aboriginal fashion designer couture, activewear, sporting apparel, textile installations in art and design contexts.

statements.statement: Explore Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ material sourcing Practices and describe the suitability of the materials for end use
examples: Wetland grasses and reeds, pandanus as a waterproof material, spinifex cultivation for basket weaving, bark fibre for string, mats, dilly bags and dance belts.

statements.statement: Investigate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander customary Practices and outline how they are applied to contemporary designs
examples: Piinpi fashion, Aboriginal textile designers, symbolism in representative sports jerseys.

statements.statement: Evaluate ethical considerations for the use and appropriation of designs and products
Explore design inspiration sources in the local area to generate textile design ideas and concepts
Apply protocols for designing with respect for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander designers, Communities and Cultural Knowledges, including Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property (ICIP)

groups.title: Historical and cultural influences on textile practices

statements.statement: Investigate textile designers and textile products from a range of historical periods
Identify and describe how historical design features can be applied to contemporary designs
Investigate reasons textile design practices have changed over time
Evaluate how textile practices have changed over time to improve sustainability
Investigate and evaluate textile practices and describe design features of textile products from a range of cultural groups
Evaluate how diverse cultural perspectives may influence the work of textile designers
Identify historical and cultural design features to apply as sources of design inspiration in the development of textile projects

groups.title: Textile industry design and production practices

statements.statement: Identify fibres cultivated in Australia for use in textile design and production
Describe local and global techniques used in the cultivation and processing of fibres
Identify and evaluate sustainable textile materials and practices
examples: Organic and vegan textiles, organic and chemical-free farming.

statements.statement: Identify textile supply chain systems to assess future development opportunities
Explain current challenges that may influence future development of Australian textile industries
examples: Climate, pest and disease management, market fluctuations, textile imports.

statements.statement: Discuss emerging opportunities to improve sustainable textile practices
examples: Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) sustainably produced fibres, waste management processes.

statements.statement: Investigate innovative technologies used in textile design and production
Investigate career opportunities in textile design and production industries
Describe the influence of globalisation on the Australian textile industry
Analyse ethical considerations for local and global textile design and production practices
Investigate community and industry initiatives that promote textile sustainability and consumer awareness
Explore ways designers and consumers can influence change in textile design and production practices to improve sustainability in the textile industry
Explain relationships between textile design, production and sustainable practices
Identify and describe different purposes of textile design
Investigate how textile designers adapt designs in response to consumer demands
Evaluate adaptive, emerging and innovative textile technologies for specific purposes
examples: Light-up safety wear, sensory-friendly clothing, temperature control clothing.

statements.statement: Describe how innovative textile design can improve accessibility, participation and inclusivity for diverse populations
Assess the functional requirements of textile products for their intended purpose
Generate textile ideas and concepts for identified needs and diverse purposes

groups.title: Material selection for textile production and end use

statements.statement: Identify a range of fibres, yarns and fabrics used in the creation of textile projects
Outline differences between natural and synthetic fibre production
Compare characteristics of yarn types, including staple and filament composition, single and plied structure, low and high twist, and other properties, including strength and texture
Identify properties and structures of fabrics, including woven, knit and non-woven
Explain how properties of fibres, yarns and fabrics determine their suitability for end use
Evaluate sustainable material sourcing practices for textile design and production
Explain the selection and suitability of materials for textile products

groups.title: Creative textile design and technological applications

statements.statement: Identify elements of design, including shape, size, colour, value, line, direction and texture
Identify principles of design, including proportion, balance, rhythm, emphasis, contrast and harmony
Describe elements and principles of design featured in works created by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
Assess how elements and principles of design feature in the works and collections of textile designers
Explore customary and contemporary decorative design Practices developed by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples
Investigate textile designs and designers that feature creative decorative applications
Generate ideas and concepts for innovative design and technological applications
Demonstrate safe and ethical practices when using digital design and technological applications
Investigate the application of innovative sustainable technologies for textile design and production
Explore elements and principles of design through practical application
Evaluate the practices and products of textile designers
Identify and describe target markets for current and emerging textile designers and brands
Compare promotional strategies used by textile designers
Investigate how data is used by textile designers and brands to inform textile product design
Explain how textile designers promote ethical and sustainable design practices
Use digital design and technological applications to create promotional materials for textile consumers
Demonstrate safe and ethical practices when accessing and collecting data
Identify textile products created within a range of different textile design areas
Outline the uses of a range of textile products
Describe aesthetic features of a range of textile products
Explain functional properties of a range of textile products
Investigate a range of design inspiration sources
Explore how designers use design inspiration sources when developing textile products and collections
Select and evaluate design inspiration sources for the development of textile projects
Outline features of design inspiration sources used to generate and refine ideas
Demonstrate safe and ethical practices using digital technologies to source information
Explore design software and applications to design and generate ideas
Apply design and creative thinking to generate ideas using a range of communication techniques
examples: Fashion drawing, production drawings, pattern pieces, sketching.

statements.statement: Annotate aesthetic features and functional properties of design ideas
Evaluate and refine design ideas to justify the selection of final textile products using written, visual, verbal or multimodal communication forms
Analyse ways that textile ideas and products could be modified to improve sustainability
Use subject-specific terminology to communicate ideas for textile design and production
Explore and experiment with construction techniques to test their suitability for textile products through practical application
Investigate and experiment with decorative techniques to enhance textile products through practical application
Evaluate experimentation with decorative and construction techniques to determine their application to textile projects
Experiment with design software and applications to decorate and manipulate materials for textile design and production
Examine fabric characteristics and properties to determine their suitability for textile products
examples: Abrasion resistance, breathability, colour, drape, durability, stretch, texture, woven, knitted, bonded, waterproof.

statements.statement: Justify the selection of materials used for textile products through testing and evaluation
Create written texts to describe and evaluate design ideas and production processes

groups.title: Textile product construction and design application

statements.statement: Apply planning and organisation skills in the production of textile products
Demonstrate safe practices when selecting and using materials, technologies and processes
Identify and apply appropriate standards and codes of practice when designing textile products
examples: Mandatory standards for safety testing and care labelling, diversity codes of practice.

statements.statement: Use collaborative practices in textile design and production, including teamwork, communication and shared decision-making
Deconstruct textile products to identify components and explore creative reuse opportunities
Identify and apply sustainable practices and processes for textile design and production
Identify and select appropriate fabric and notions for production
Select, modify and use construction patterns
examples: Commercial patterns, drafting blocks, digital pattern making applications.

statements.statement: Interpret pattern instructions, transfer pattern marking and apply pattern layout plans
Select and apply construction techniques to develop quality textile products
Select and apply decorative techniques to enhance textile designs
examples: Colouration, embellishment, fabric manipulation, haberdashery applications.

statements.statement: Apply ongoing evaluation during the development and production of textile products
Develop, refine and demonstrate technical proficiency through textile project work, individually or collaboratively

boundaries.note: The syllabus establishes curriculum requirements; current local demonstrations, plans, equipment, PPE, risk controls and supervision authorise practical delivery.
Local cultural knowledge, permissions and collaboration protocols remain with the relevant Aboriginal Community and teacher-approved sources.
